headline: Protein language model embeddings for structural similarity and interaction prediction
label: Learned Molecular Interaction Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and a published study test whether learned embeddings generalize to unseen molecules and remote structural relationships.
synthesis: Across these items, learned representations either replace or augment alignment-based or observed-edge features. A preprint benchmarks four protein language model embeddings (ESM-1b, ESM-2, ProtT5, ProstT5) for alignment-free structural similarity in the protein-sequence twilight zone, using cosine comparison. A second preprint, persistent manifold learning, combines multiscale interface manifolds and graph Laplacian topological features with language model embeddings to characterize protein properties. The published PRInter framework applies inductive multimodal heterogeneous network embedding with contrastive learning to predict lncRNA-protein interactions for unseen molecules. What is new here is the emphasis on inductive generalization and on topology-derived features layered onto sequence-derived embeddings.
